name: Politically Incorrect

tenures.role: tag team — PCW Tag Team Champions (won via a Gauntlet Match, 30 Mar 2002; lost to The Heartbreakers, 11 May 2002); also part-owners of PCW itself and its heel faction "The Ultimate Authority" (with Xavier Kannon and Tim Walden), running interference for owner Tyler Nelson
tenures.source: the team's own PCW biography (promotions/pcw/archive/politically-incorrect-bio.html), including its own dated 16-match PCW Match History (8 Mar – 7 Jun 2002), and OSW's own roleplay message archive (roleplays/messages/948.shtml, Wayback capture, 18 Nov 2002 — Powell's in-character “I own ten percent of Primetime Championship Wrestling” line naming the PCW part-ownership and the Ultimate Authority faction)
tenures.note: The bio's own match log runs 16 matches, Fri. Fusion 8 Mar 2002 through Fri. Fusion 7 Jun 2002: opened with tag wins over Bobby Stormbringer/DarkStar and Misplaced, lost a first Tag Team Title shot to Golden Game (interference from The Chef), then won the titles outright in a Gauntlet Match (Fear Factory, Misplaced, Metallyx, Cowabunga Connection, Golden Game, in that order) and retained in a fourway dance at Spring Fling before losing them clean to The Heartbreakers at PCW Supremacy. Two of the team's own build-up roleplays are served in full: promotions/pcw/rp/facing-ones-fears.html (27 Mar 2002, ahead of the Gauntlet Match) and promotions/pcw/rp/aquiring-transportation.html (7 Apr 2002).

tenures.role: challengers, then co-holders of the United States Championship (25 May - 29 June 2003), and members of the Red Army, managed by Alexei Ruslan; challenged Heaven & Hell for the OSW World Tag Team Championship, Falls Count Anywhere, 9 Feb 2003 Slam!, and lost when the Reverend Jon Hull intervened on the champions' behalf
tenures.source: promotions/osw/archive/slam-2003-02-09.html (served, primary source); the fed's own title history (/promotions/osw/archive/ose-title-history-wrestling-site-july-2003-2003-07-21.html); the team's own card of 20 June 2003 (/promotions/osw/archive/politically-incorrect-tag-team-card-june-2003-2003-06-20.html); the Red Army stable page of 14 January 2004 (/promotions/osw/archive/red-army-stable-january-2004-2004-01-14.html), which still lists them, active
tenures.note: OSW's own title history (captured 21 July 2003) records them declared co-holders of the United States Championship on 25 May 2003, when Powell and Lovecraft made a simultaneous pin on D-Kay Calyx in the Chaos In The Cage Match, and losing it to Azala Zameer at Ascension on 29 June 2003. No OSW page held puts the World Tag Team Championship on them. Vintage Wrestling's own unpublished 2004 segment draft has two OSW wrestlers, Farwell and Walkins, recall defeating Politically Incorrect and P.W.A. in a “No Ladders II” match for the OSW Tag Team Titles; no OSW document held carries that match, and it puts no OSW title on this team.

tenures.role: tag team: FSW Tag Team Champions from Bad Moon Rising, 20 October 2002, to Glory 20, 27 November 2002; first seen masked as the Dead Presidents, 22 August 2002
tenures.source: Five Star Wrestling's own backstage database (lot 0159): the show write-ups of 22 August to 27 November 2002; bios 7976 and 10190
tenures.note: Appears first as the masked Dead Presidents (Nixon and Kennedy) on 22 August 2002 and takes the FSW Tag Team Championship from Bad Frotitude in a chain match at Bad Moon Rising on 20 October 2002, where the masks come off: “WILLIAM S. POWELL!!”, “REGINALD V. LOVECRAFT!”, “AND THEIR CAMPAIGN MANAGER, ROGER SCHULTZ……THE NEW FSW TAG TEAM CHAMPIONS, POLITICALLY…INCORRECT!” They keep the titles on 30 October (Magnum Wolf pulls the referee out and signals for the disqualification: “PI RETAIN!”), 6 November (the timekeeper, on the time limit: “the winners of this match and still FSW Tag Team Champions”) and 13 November (beaten by disqualification: “still your tag team champions”), run the Supreme Court stable with Magnum Wolf and Big Daveylicious, and lose the titles on 27 November 2002, at Glory 20, to Jason McAllister and Neurosis (“The new FSW Tag Team Champions walk up the aisle”). The show is the fed's last in the record.

caption: William S. Powell and Reginald V. Lovecraft, PCW's own Tag Team Champions and part-owners, who held the FSW Tag Team Championship from 20 October to 27 November 2002 and OSW's United States Championship, as co-holders, from 25 May to 29 June 2003.

identity.note: PCW's own database (lot 0159) carries this team's own PCW biography card, bio 823, whose roster names the same two members already recorded here. One discrepancy stands rather than being resolved: that database bills the second member Reginald P. Lovecraft where the served biography page reads Reginald V. Lovecraft. Its appearance record covers a narrower window than the PCW tenure held here, which rests on the team's own title reign, so the dates are unchanged.

name: Dream Syndicate

tenures.style: Basho is opposite to Ukyo, a shoot-fighter based tactician. He revolves his offense around a Ground and Pound technique, take the opponent down with technical maneuvers and beat him into submission with stiff strikes. He uses his share of power moves, not to mention a few hard kicks to the chin and face to knock the opponent down. His defense involves reversing grapples, and countering strikes with harder strikes of his own. In Japan he used to be known as "Three Strikes" because no one could stand against his three-strike combo; no one has been left standing.

identity.note: The same stable under the same invented styling in two federations. Ultra Fantasy Wrestling's own Stables page carries sHs with Revenant and Scott “The Hott One” Naket named and a third place left TBA; PCW's own database carries sHs with Scott Naket, Revenant, Kris Kanton and The Preacher. Both named members are the same two men, whose own records merge on their own receipts, and “sHs” — lower case, upper case, lower case — is nobody's archetype. PCW's own Fusion of 13 October 2000 puts an Ultra Fantasy Wrestling arrival on its air in “that stupid sHs tee-shirt” five weeks after that federation closed. One stable, carried over, with two members added on the far side.

identity.note: Shares the billed name "The Think Tank" with james-rollins-swift-mma; nothing in either record joins them, and a shared ring name alone establishes no identity.

PCW's own Fusion of 25 May 2001 says the stable predates PCW and says where: Alan Kriegman claims the dressing room as “the one who carried this stable The first time it was around”, Professor Herbert D. Dorkiman answers “Were you in UFW with Nick, Howard and I?”, and Kriegman concedes — “The first time around here in PCW.” Ultra Fantasy Wrestling's own Stables page carries the Think Tank with exactly those three, Howard Porter, Dorkiman and Nick Taylor, two of them champions on the day it closed. Its own final member list also carries the fourth PCW member, billed “Brian Gaines, The Chosen One”. One stable across two federations, membership recorded by era, with Kriegman joining only on the far side by his own admission. Folds in the separately-filed Ultra Fantasy Wrestling record for the same stable, the-think-tank-ufw-ultra-2000, which retires forward.
OSW's own card for the Think Tank (bio 4593) narrates the stable's PCW history (its PCW feuds and the 'Commissioner' reveal), which is the PCW stable this record holds.
